Reference scores and count definitions

Pooled cells: 600 assignments; lexical cells: 300; controls: 100. Pooled and lexical views overlap. Controls are reused across matched comparisons. Missing-pair Δ bounds use [0,1] and equal-task weighting.

Uncertainty, tests and correlation definitions

Each effect is the equal-original-task mean of paired treatment − reference differences. Shared controls and all wording variants remain together within original-task clusters; cells and lexical variants are not independent extra observations. Unknown scores remain unknown, and intervals condition on observed pairs rather than imputing missing scores.

Two-sided paired condition-label permutation tests assume the sharp exchangeability null across condition labels within each original task. They retain the actual 6:1 pooled (or 3:1 lexical) treatment-setting / reference imbalance, samples and task variants. Missing paired outcomes retain their observed-pair estimate and bootstrap CI but have no permutation p-value. Holm adjustment uses all 112 planned effects (2 models × 7 beliefs × 2 methods × 4 benchmarks) for the selected protocol / wording / reference view, including non-estimable cells. Display filters do not reduce that family. Alternative overlapping views are separate exploratory families, not globally corrected across view choices.

Pearson correlations describe matched effect profiles, not independent-task observations. Per-benchmark correlations condition on the selected method(s). The pooled correlation mixes native metrics and is descriptive only. Correlation CIs are pointwise exploratory joint task-bootstrap intervals, not multiplicity-adjusted; no iid-cell Pearson p-value is reported. Constant profiles have undefined correlation. Insufficient valid bootstrap draws yield no interval.

Directional counts use only pairs with both effects nonzero (tolerance 10⁻¹²); one-zero and both-zero pairs are reported separately. No task variation or a zero-width empirical interval does not establish zero population uncertainty. These summaries do not establish latent belief uptake or causality.
